newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi praises Albania PM for deal on polls.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi praises Albania PM for deal on polls.

text.p: ROME, May 10 (Rueter) - Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi praised an agreement to hold early elections in Albania when he met the Balkan country's interim prime minister Bashkim Fino on Saturday.

Prodi and Fino, who were both accompanied by their foreign, finance and justice misters, met at Rome's Ciampino military airport during a brief stopover in the Albanian delegation's trip to Washington.

Their five-day trip to the United States starts a day after European envoy Franz Vranitzky secured an agreement from Albania's 10 main political parties to break an impasse in holding early elections in late June.

"This (early polls) was one of the main goals of our mission in Albania," Prodi said told news conference, adding that he had spoken on Friday with Albanian President Sali Berisha, who confirmed his "full support" for the elections.

Italy commands a 6,000-strong force with a three-month U.N. mandate to secure the delivery of humanitarian aid in the impoverished Balkan state following its slide towards anarchy in March after the collapse of dubious savings schemes.

On Friday, Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta was quoted as saying that Italy could seek a wider mandate for the multinational security force to help oversee the elections if an agreement to hold them was reached.

Fino, who said before leaving Tirana that he would seek assistance from the United States in holding the elections, called the agreement "an excellent outcome" and thanked Prodi for the role that Italy was playing in Albania.

"You are also helping to create the right economic conditions for the future and the government that will come after the polls," said Fino, who heads a nine-party government of National Reconciliation set up in March to halt Albania's drift to anarchy.
He said it was now the government's responsibility to make sure the election campaign was carried out in a stabile and non-violent enviornment.
"For the elections, we want to collaborate with all the local authorities -- we are not interested in groups who are asking for the resignation of the government or of President Berisha," he said.

Fino will meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Monday, and has said he will also see congressmen, senators, senior politicians, businessmen and heads of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
